name: Accessory Navicular Syndrome
definition: Symptomatic accessory navicular, usually causing medial midfoot pain from irritation at the posterior tibial tendon insertion or shoe pressure.

investigations.principle: Radiographs identify accessory navicular; MRI is used when edema/tendon pathology needs clarification.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, inflammatory, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

amber: Persistent symptomatic cases may require excision/reconstruction.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Pada/Asthi-Snayu phenotype may be documented descriptively.

patientEducation.summary: Symptomatic accessory navicular, usually causing medial midfoot pain from irritation at the posterior tibial tendon insertion or shoe pressure.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
